introduction.value: Test suite for ChibiOS OS Library. The purpose of this suite is to perform unit tests on the library modules and to converge to 100% code coverage through successive improvements.

description.value: This sequence reports configuration and version information about the OS library.
Port-related info are reported.
Prints the version string.
The version numbers are reported.
Prints the version string.
The static OS Library settings are reported.
Prints the configuration options settings.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to mailboxes.
The mailbox normal API is tested without triggering blocking conditions.
Testing the mailbox size.

code.value: test_assert_lock(chMBGetFreeCountI(&mb1) == MB_SIZE, "wrong size");

description.value: Resetting the mailbox, conditions are checked, no errors expected.
Testing the behavior of API when the mailbox is in reset state then return in active state.
Filling the mailbox using chMBPostTimeout() and chMBPostAheadTimeout() once, no errors expected.
Testing intermediate conditions. Data pointers must be aligned, semaphore counters are checked.
Emptying the mailbox using chMBFetchTimeout(), no errors expected.
Posting and then fetching one more message, no errors expected.
Testing final conditions. Data pointers must be aligned to buffer start, semaphore counters are checked.
The mailbox I-Class API is tested without triggering blocking conditions.
Testing the mailbox size.

code.value: test_assert_lock(chMBGetFreeCountI(&mb1) == MB_SIZE, "wrong size");

description.value: Resetting the mailbox, conditions are checked, no errors expected. The mailbox is then returned in active state.
Filling the mailbox using chMBPostI() and chMBPostAheadI() once, no errors expected.
Testing intermediate conditions. Data pointers must be aligned, semaphore counters are checked.
Emptying the mailbox using chMBFetchI(), no errors expected.
Posting and then fetching one more message, no errors expected.
Testing final conditions. Data pointers must be aligned to buffer start, semaphore counters are checked.
The mailbox API is tested for timeouts.
Filling the mailbox.
Testing chMBPostTimeout(), chMBPostI(), chMBPostAheadTimeout() and chMBPostAheadI() timeout.
Resetting the mailbox. The mailbox is then returned in active state.

code.value: chMBReset(&mb1); chMBResumeX(&mb1);

description.value: Testing chMBFetchTimeout() and chMBFetchI() timeout.
Repeated post-ahead operations wrap from the buffer base and decrement within the buffer. Capacities from one to four messages are checked using both S-class and I-class APIs.
Fill and drain each capacity repeatedly using S-class post-ahead. Check read pointer positions, full rejection, reverse message order and the final empty state.
Repeat the capacity and wraparound checks using I-class post-ahead and fetch operations.
All three FIFO receive variants return the original object pointers through pointer-typed output variables.
Post objects and receive them using the I-class API, checking pointer identity and restoring the free pool.
Repeat the pointer round-trip check using the S-class receive API.
Repeat the pointer round-trip check using the ordinary receive API.
Immediate and finite receive timeouts leave the caller's output pointer unchanged.
Receive from an empty FIFO using the I-class API. The timeout must not overwrite the output pointer.
Check unchanged output for both immediate and finite timeouts using the S-class receive API.
Check unchanged output for both immediate and finite timeouts using the ordinary receive API.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to pipes.
The pipe functionality is tested by loading and emptying it, all conditions are tested.
Resetting pipe.
Writing data, must fail.
Reading data, must fail.
Reactivating pipe.
Filling whole pipe.
Emptying pipe.
Small write.
Filling remaining space.
Small Read.
Reading remaining data.
Small Write.
Small Read.
Write wrapping buffer boundary.
Read wrapping buffer boundary.
The pipe API is tested for timeouts.
Reading while pipe is empty.
Writing a string larger than pipe buffer.
Readers and writers exchange data through a pipe smaller than the request. All waits are bounded.
A waiting reader receives a multi-chunk write.
A waiting writer completes a multi-chunk read.
Reset aborts the current waiter and prevents a caller queued on the direction lock from transferring or waiting again. Cleanup precedes assertions, and worker waits are bounded.
Both a suspended reader and a queued reader stop after one reset.
A queued writer cannot repopulate a reset pipe.

brief.value: Partial pipe transfers interrupted by reset.

description.value: An already-suspended caller returns its partial count, even when the pipe is resumed before the caller runs.
Reset preserves the partial read count.
Reset preserves the partial write count.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to Jobs Queues.
The dispatcher API is tested for functionality.
Initializing the Jobs Queue object.

code.value: chJobObjectInit(&jq, JOBS_QUEUE_SIZE, jobs, msg_queue);

description.value: Starting the dispatcher threads.
Sending jobs with various timings.
Sending two null jobs to make threads exit.
Verifying that all descriptors have been returned.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to Thread Delegates.
The dispatcher API is tested for functionality.
Starting the dispatcher thread.
Calling the default veneers, checking the result and the emitted tokens.
Waiting for the thread to terminate-

code.value: msg_t msg = chThdWait(tp); test_assert(msg == 0x0FA5, "invalid exit code");

description.value: Empty immediate and finite delegate waits return timeout.
Polling with no pending call returns immediately.

code.value:
msg_t msg = chDelegateDispatchTimeout(TIME_IMMEDIATE);
test_assert(msg == MSG_TIMEOUT, "unexpected poll result");

description.value: A finite wait with no caller expires.
Immediate dispatch processes a queued call, and finite and infinite waits process calls arriving later. Each caller receives the callback result.
Dispatching calls with immediate, finite and infinite waits, then joining the callers before checking results.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to Objects Caches.
A cache object is initialized, some initial conditions are checked.
Cache initialization.

code.value: chCacheObjectInit(&cache1, NUM_HASH_ENTRIES, hash_elements, NUM_OBJECTS, sizeof (cached_object_t), objects, obj_read, obj_write);

description.value: Getting and releasing objects without initialization.
Getting and releasing objects with synchronous initialization.
Getting and releasing objects with asynchronous initialization.
Checking cached objects.
Checking non-cached objects.
Repeated cached hits followed by a miss.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to memory pools.

brief.value: Loading and emptying a memory pool.

description.value: The memory pool functionality is tested by loading and emptying it, all conditions are tested.
Adding the objects to the pool using chPoolLoadArray().

code.value: chPoolLoadArray(&mp1, objects, MEMORY_POOL_SIZE);

description.value: Emptying the pool using chPoolAlloc().

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) test_assert(chPoolAlloc(&mp1) != NULL, "list empty");

description.value: Now must be empty.

code.value: test_assert(chPoolAlloc(&mp1) == NULL, "list not empty");

description.value: Adding the objects to the pool using chPoolFree().

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) chPoolFree(&mp1, &objects[i]);

description.value: Emptying the pool using chPoolAlloc() again.

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) test_assert(chPoolAlloc(&mp1) != NULL, "list empty");

description.value: Now must be empty again.

code.value: test_assert(chPoolAlloc(&mp1) == NULL, "list not empty");

description.value: Covering the case where a provider is unable to return more memory.

code.value: chPoolObjectInit(&mp1, sizeof (uintptr_t), null_provider); test_assert(chPoolAlloc(&mp1) == NULL, "provider returned memory");

brief.value: Loading and emptying a guarded memory pool without waiting.

description.value: The memory pool functionality is tested by loading and emptying it, all conditions are tested.
Adding the objects to the pool using chGuardedPoolLoadArray().

code.value: chGuardedPoolLoadArray(&gmp1, objects, MEMORY_POOL_SIZE);

description.value: Emptying the pool using chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout().

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) test_assert(chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout(&gmp1, TIME_IMMEDIATE) != NULL, "list empty");

description.value: Now must be empty.

code.value: test_assert(chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout(&gmp1, TIME_IMMEDIATE) == NULL, "list not empty");

description.value: Adding the objects to the pool using chGuardedPoolFree().

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) chGuardedPoolFree(&gmp1, &objects[i]);

description.value: Emptying the pool using chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout() again.

code.value: for (i = 0; i < MEMORY_POOL_SIZE; i++) test_assert(chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout(&gmp1, TIME_IMMEDIATE) != NULL, "list empty");

description.value: Now must be empty again.

code.value: test_assert(chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout(&gmp1, TIME_IMMEDIATE) == NULL, "list not empty");

description.value: The timeout features for the Guarded Memory Pools is tested.
Trying to allocate with 100mS timeout, must fail because the pool is empty.

code.value: test_assert(chGuardedPoolAllocTimeout(&gmp1, TIME_MS2I(100)) == NULL, "list not empty");

description.value: This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to memory heaps.

Series of allocations/deallocations are performed in carefully designed sequences in order to stimulate all the possible code paths inside the allocator. The test expects to find the heap back to the initial status after each sequence.
Testing initial conditions, the heap must not be fragmented and one free block present, finally, integrity is checked.

code.value: test_assert(chHeapStatus(&test_heap, &sz, NULL) == 1, "heap fragmented"); test_assert(!chHeapIntegrityCheck(&test_heap), "integrity failure");

description.value: Trying to allocate an block bigger than available space, an error is expected, finally, integrity is checked.
Single block allocation using chHeapAlloc() then the block is freed using chHeapFree(), must not fail, finally, integrity is checked.
Using chHeapStatus() to assess the heap state. There must be at least one free block of sufficient size, finally, integrity is checked.
Allocating then freeing in the same order, finally, integrity is checked.
Allocating then freeing in reverse order, finally, integrity is checked.
Small fragments handling. Checking the behavior when allocating blocks with size not multiple of alignment unit, finally, integrity is checked.
Skipping a fragment, the first fragment in the list is too small so the allocator must pick the second one, finally, integrity is checked.
Allocating the whole available space, finally, integrity is checked.
Testing final conditions. The heap geometry must be the same than the one registered at beginning, finally, integrity is checked.
The default heap is pre-allocated in the system. We test base functionality.
Single block allocation using chHeapAlloc() then the block is freed using chHeapFree(), must not fail.
Testing allocation failure.

code.value: p1 = chHeapAlloc(NULL, (size_t)-256); test_assert(p1 == NULL, "allocation not failed");

description.value: The integrity checker rejects headers outside the heap or only partially contained in it. All test headers have valid backing storage, so no fault or kernel assertion is expected.
The initial heap must pass the integrity check.

code.value: test_assert(!chHeapIntegrityCheck(&test_heap), "initial integrity failure");

description.value: A header below the heap base must be rejected. Restore the link before checking the result.
A header at the first address beyond the heap must be rejected. Restore the link before checking the result.
A header whose final byte is outside the heap must be rejected. Restore the area before checking the result.
An out-of-area link after a valid header must also be rejected. Restore the link before checking the result.
Block sizes must be representable in bytes and fit the heap area. Invalid page counts are restored before checking test results.
The initial block ending exactly at the heap limit must pass the check.

code.value: test_assert(!chHeapIntegrityCheck(&test_heap), "exact-fit block rejected");

description.value: A page count that would wrap the byte size to one header must be rejected.
A page count whose header addition would wrap must be rejected.
The first page count whose full byte size cannot be represented must be rejected.
A representable byte size that exceeds this heap must still be rejected.
A block exceeding the heap by one page must be rejected.
Free block extents must not overlap, while separated blocks and zero-page fragments remain valid. Link-order and loop checks must be preserved.
Ascending headers whose blocks overlap by one header must be rejected even though both blocks fit individually in the heap.
Separated free blocks, including one ending at the heap limit, must pass the check.
An allocation leaving a zero-page tail fragment must pass the check, as must the heap after freeing it.
Self-links and backward links must still be rejected without looping.
This sequence tests the ChibiOS library functionalities related to the object factory.
This test case verifies the static objects registry.
Retrieving a registered object by name, must not exist.

code.value: rop = chFactoryFindObject("myobj"); test_assert(rop == NULL, "found");

description.value: Registering an object, it must not exists, must succeed.
Registering an object with the same name, must fail.
Retrieving the registered object by name, must exist, then increasing the reference counter, finally releasing both references.
Releasing the first reference to the object, must not trigger an assertion.

code.value: chFactoryReleaseObject(rop);

description.value: Retrieving the registered object by name again, must not exist.

code.value: rop = chFactoryFindObject("myobj"); test_assert(rop == NULL, "found");

code.value: dbp = chFactoryFindBuffer("mybuf"); test_assert(dbp == NULL, "found");

description.value: This sequence tests core allocation boundaries and verifies that failed requests leave the allocator unchanged.
Base allocation rejects oversized requests and accounts for prefix and alignment space before accepting a block.
A maximum-size request with a prefix must fail without changing either boundary.
A maximum-size prefix must fail without changing either boundary.
A request one byte larger than the arena must fail without changing either boundary.
Alignment must leave room for both the returned pointer and the requested bytes.
An exact fit including prefix and alignment padding must succeed.
An empty aligned arena accepts a zero-size request but rejects a nonzero request.
Top allocation rejects oversized requests and accounts for prefix and alignment space before accepting a block.
A near-maximum prefix must fail without changing either boundary.
A maximum-size request must fail without changing either boundary.
A prefix that exceeds the remaining space by one byte must fail without changing either boundary.
Alignment must leave room for both the returned pointer and the prefix.
An exact fit including prefix and alignment padding must succeed.
An empty aligned arena accepts a zero-size request but rejects a nonzero request.
Memory area intersections, bounded scans and API availability are tested independently of the optional system memory checks.
Both intersection APIs are checked in both argument orders for nested, overlapping, equal and disjoint areas.
Strict enclosure intersects in both directions.
Partial overlap intersects in both directions.
Equal areas intersect.
Separated and adjacent areas do not intersect.
The last byte is included but the following byte is not.
Whole-address-space and boundary ranges preserve symmetric intersection semantics without accessing memory.
The whole address space intersects an ordinary area and itself.
The byte at address zero is part of the whole address space.
Nested areas ending at the highest address intersect.
Adjacent areas near the highest address do not intersect.
An area ending at the highest address intersects the whole address space.
A pointer-array scan must fit complete pointer slots inside both the byte budget and the containing area.
Even an empty array needs a complete NULL pointer within the byte budget.
Every budget ending before the complete terminator is rejected, including non-multiples of pointer size.
An exact or larger budget returns the complete array size, including its terminator.
The byte budget is relative to the candidate array, not the containing area's base.
A large budget cannot admit a partial terminator or an unterminated array at the area boundary.
String and area-table checks remain available when system memory checks are disabled.
A string check includes the terminator and rejects a byte budget that is too short.
The terminated area table accepts a contained range and rejects a larger one.
The public permission-check APIs remain callable and return true when system memory checks are disabled.
Read, write and executable-address fallbacks use the same public names as the enabled APIs.
Strings and pointer arrays in separate objects are rejected in both address orders without ordering pointers.
A string in another object is outside the area, in either argument order.
A pointer array in another object is outside the area, in either argument order.
Scans obey finite byte-area boundaries without forming typed pointers from those boundaries.
A string suffix must fit the area and budget, including the terminating byte.
Byte-area boundaries need not have pointer alignment, but each scanned pointer must fit completely.
A whole-address-space map accepts valid strings and pointer arrays while preserving their byte budgets.
Strings still require a budget large enough for the terminator, including with a whole-space map.
A missing string terminator is rejected at the byte budget without reading beyond the backing array.
Pointer arrays require complete slots within the budget, including the NULL terminator.
A missing NULL pointer is rejected at the byte budget without reading beyond the backing array.
Address zero is a valid range-query value, while zero size denotes the whole space only when the address is zero.
A whole-space table entry contains the whole space and the first and last addressable bytes.
Zero size with a nonzero base is not a whole-space query, and a range crossing the address limit is rejected.
A finite area at address zero contains that byte but cannot contain the whole address space.
Enabled read/write wrappers accept address-zero queries and use the configured permission tables.
Whole-space queries agree with the configured readable and writable area tables.
Single-byte address-zero queries agree with the configured readable and writable area tables.
